coverage: All 24 cards start without selected answers and complete through real element choices
Reversed endpoints and line order, alternative valid plane triples, coordinate aliases and reversed half-length parallel direction

independentProbes.kind: Exhaustive parallel-action candidate enumeration after the fix
independentProbes.result: PASS: only transfer through P in the direction MN is accepted for the current known points; reversed direction and edge endpoints also pass

independentProbes.kind: Exhaustive pairs of lines through currently known points
independentProbes.result: PASS: only the intended geometric intersections are accepted; no analogous accidental-coordinate acceptance found in the bounded bank

findings.finding: Authored step titles disclosed expected endpoints, roles or planes before a choice.
findings.resolution: Neutral titles and task-specific route goals replace the revealing titles; prompts do not provide the correct role. Route goals identify a meaningful order without requiring guesses about the author's order.

findings.finding: The location-field label disclosed the authored target edge before line selection.
findings.resolution: The label asks about a finite edge or its extension without printing the expected edge.

findings.finding: bridge-19 accepted a line through A parallel to GM, or through E parallel to CM, because it happened to hit Q; rendering then substituted the authored PQ action.
findings.resolution: Validation now requires an anchor on the actual section trace and a direction parallel to the established trace. Both false examples are rejected; geometric alias and scaled/reversed equivalents remain accepted. Rendering records the accepted anchor.

findings.finding: In bridge-06/20, accepted intersection text and geometry revealed YP and its section role before the subsequent endpoint/role choice.
findings.resolution: Confirmation and history describe only accepted selections. Intersections render chosen helper lines and the found point; YP becomes a section side only after its own accepted choice and disappears on undo.

findings.finding: Deferring section classification also required preserving the final QP boundary in bridge-18/24.
findings.resolution: QP is drawn as a section side after explicit confirmation of the complete boundary; editing the boundary removes that confirmation and classification.

stateAndBoardAssessment: PASS within the reviewed scope: saved action prefixes are revalidated; help and earned history remain sticky; undo removes an actual action; old guided records are retained; construction is disabled on the board and does not enter its existing strict state schema.
limitations: Mathematical probes cover the approved fixed bank, not an arbitrary construction editor.
The application checks geometric selections; it does not automatically grade a complete proof.
Browser-harness inspection was static. Real browser rendering, visual acceptance and production acceptance are separate gates.
This is internal independent review evidence, not a review from an external model provider and not release authorization.

reviewedDeltas.regression: Navigation from the completed eight-step auth-method-04 to five-step auth-metric-09 preserves state, storage and SVG under delayed detached toggles; live construction, rotation and flat view on the new lesson still work.

reviewedDeltas.change: After the existing two placement passes, an overlapping label may move to an unoccupied location on a bounded six-pixel grid inside the SVG frame.
reviewedDeltas.assessment: PASS: fallback runs only for a colliding padded box, rejects every candidate overlapping another label or point, preserves the label and font, and retains the existing leader connection. It does not change model coordinates, edges, action state or displayed label membership.
reviewedDeltas.regression: The actual CI glyph-width fixture for the dense 267-by-205 prism SVG retains all 26 labels and points, with no clipped painted labels, label-to-label overlaps or glyph-to-point overlaps.
